headline: The bombers that were never really there
lede: MISSILE BATTLE's autopilot has been politely declining to shoot bombers since it shipped. Digging in found two stacked causes: the decision branch was unreachable whenever a bomber flew alone, and the wave scripts' declared cruise altitudes were never compiled — the audit verified numbers the sim ignored, so bombers cruised invisible above the aim band, unkillable by anyone. The autopilot now hunts loaded bombers on purpose and denies every delivery in the game.

notes.text: #2306 shipped: the autopilot hunts bombers when nothing needs answering — legal only while tube ammo covers the open-threat reserve. Proven run: 49 interceptors (was 60), all four bombers bagged, all 14 scripted drops denied before delivery, zero cities lost, and every wave still wins with one fewer interceptor per battery.

missilecheck gains a BOMBER HUNT section (9 pins): spawned altitude must equal the script's declared one and sit inside the aim band, a NaN altitude throws at spawn, a quiet-sky kill at 3 rounds/tube (below the old gate), a held-tube refusal, and whole-game denial counts. Two named manual mutants; 378/378 green; missileplay 26/26 with zero page errors.

A spec field is not a fact until the sim compiles it. The altitude was declared, audited and ignored — the gate printed 14/14 legal while the world had none. Pin spawned state against the spec, not the spec against itself.

An early-return can shadow a whole branch: `if (!live.length) return {}` made the bomber doctrine unreachable exactly when it mattered, and weeks of honest README notes described code that could not run.
